task: T-136 — is there a FLAT 30-root placement?
conditions: T = 300 K, k_BT = 4.141947 pN nm; aqueous 2 mM MgCl2; 40.0 x 40.35 nm single-layer square-lattice Rothemund sheet, 15 duplexes at 2.69 nm, 0.34 nm rise; C-0022's SOLVED edge profiles at 10 nm and 7 nm, both at 0.192 V; C-0017's 33.3333 pN/nm mandate as a SUM over 30 equal paths; C-0039's exact elastica arm 7.77049 nm on a one-crossover root and C-0034's A2 tip; C-0053's footprint convention at d = 2.69 nm; free-tile stroke 4.90731 nm
decision: the best two-per-row 30-root placement dishes 0.1667 of the free-tile stroke over the design device's whole range and 0.1667 at the design state, with a plan margin of 0.4195 nm — against T-5b's 0.10 and C-0072's 0.2603 / 1.3495 nm

bounds.settles: C-0063's bound 1 read at the other cap: 2 x 15 = 30 exactly, so every row carries two and the two-per-row CONSTRAINT is an IDENTITY — the design space is a product of per-row 2-subsets and nothing else, before any solve

predicates.name: the recommendation
predicates.statement: the 30-root placement that keeps every nanometre of plan margin the lattice affords AND is flattest under C-0017's unchanged total
predicates.verdict: phase 8 — the LARGEST plan ceiling, flatness unconstrained — plan margin 1.7645 nm (5.19 base-pair rises, 68.9x C-0069's 0.02561 nm knife edge and 1.31x C-0072's 1.3495 nm), dishing 0.0682 over the design device's whole range at a peak stiffness ratio of 2.06 and a peak path force of 6.857 pN against the 10 pN unzip allowable; with EQUAL springs the same placement dishes 0.2424 and is NOT flat

predicates.name: the declared falsifier
predicates.statement: no two-per-row placement clears 0.10, at either objective and at any phase, with EQUAL springs
predicates.verdict: FIRED for equal springs — no two-per-row placement of any phase clears 0.10 with them, the best being 0.1667; a DISTRIBUTION recovers it, so the trade is between an equal-spring design and a quotable margin, not between flatness and margin

findings: The two-per-row constraint at 30 roots on 15 duplexes is an IDENTITY and not a constraint: 2 x 15 = 30 exactly, so every row carries two and the whole design space is a product of per-row 2-subsets. That is C-0063's bound 1 read at the other cap, it costs one line of arithmetic, and it shrinks the centro-symmetric family from C-0063's 361 584 at 34 roots to 69984 at 30 — small enough to enumerate EXHAUSTIVELY at both phases the congruence admits.

A plan ceiling is a property of a PLACEMENT, not of a count. C-0072 reports 9.12 nm at 30 roots and 20.00 nm at 15; the largest any placement of those counts can keep on the same lattice is 9.5350 nm and 30.8800 nm. The difference is a bisection on a monotone capacity — rows are independent and a placement's ceiling is a MIN over them — so it is a proof and not a search, and it costs no solve at all.

The flatness answer for EQUAL springs: NO 30-root placement is flat with equal springs, at any of the 32 phases. Over the range the placed 2 mM / 10 nm / 0.192 V device traverses, the best two-per-row placement dishes 0.1667 (exhaustive centro-symmetric) and 0.1670 (32-phase descent) against T-5b's 0.10, C-0072's plan-rule 0.2603, C-0063's 34-root 0.0789 and a free tile at 0.3079.

The winner sits at phase 24, dishes 0.1667 at the design state and 0.1667 over the range, and carries a plan margin of 0.4195 nm — 1.23 base-pair rises against C-0072's 3.97. Per path it carries 3.333 pN of the 100 pN duty against the 10 pN unzip allowable, 2.797 pN solved and 0.392 pN of C-0014 thermal force.

The cheap bound did not decide it: the least-squares floor over EVERY phase-24 upward root is 0.0007 at the design state and 0.0005 at the compressed end, 140.5x below T-5b's convention, so the falsifier could not fire before the enumeration and the enumeration was necessary.

And the negative belongs to the EQUAL SPRINGS, not to the station set: the 30-parameter minimax at C-0017's unchanged total takes the same placements to 0.0732, 0.0648, 0.0682, 0.0648, 0.0715, 0.0894, 0.1319, 0.0894, 0.1124. So a flat 30-root design EXISTS, and it needs a distribution. C-0063's own advantage was that 34 roots need no distribution at all; at 30 that advantage is what is spent, which is CH-0080's finding on a new axis — the equal-spring advantage belongs to a COUNT as well as to a layer.

And the margin becomes QUOTABLE: all five of C-0072's floors — four of them needing no fabrication measurement and the fifth being the only one there is — are cleared at the recommended placement, the base-pair rise — the design qu at 0.3400 nm, the two measured SAXS interhelical at 0.0400 nm, the thermal axial breathing of the at 0.2654 nm, the arm tip's own bending at a PER at 1.6782 nm, Fischer et al.'s fitted single-lay at 0.2500 nm, the weakest by 1.05x. Two of them scale with the arm and are re-evaluated here rather than carried across: the arm tip's own bending at a rigid root falls from 1.8074 to 1.6782 nm as the arm shortens from 8.164 to 7.7705 nm, which is the whole of that clearance.
